habitat: The common bushveld cisticola, also in thornveld and coastal bush. It sings from the top of a bush and forages low in tangled grass and bush.
summary: A very common resident. Newman says it is robust and has few distinguishing plumage marks, with only slight seasonal differences, and that it is best told by habitat, behaviour and song. The male’s song is chi chi chi ch-r-r-r-r-r, ending in a rattle. The alarm is cheer, cheer, cheer.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^18=262144 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 131072–524288.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

viewNotes.note: Sings from the top of a bush. Few plumage marks were named.

calls.description: The male’s song is chi chi chi ch-r-r-r-r-r, the last syllable a rattle. The alarm is cheer, cheer, cheer. Grade A from Kruger. A higher-ranked Kruger file was not used because its filename says Cisticola-cf. This file’s name shows a 500 Hz high-pass applied by the recordist.
